tooltip: Stops execution with the x86 HLT instruction. The machine remains halted until an interrupt or reset, depending on interrupt state.
Puts the processor into a low-work wait state until an interrupt arrives.
Draws a string using the built-in framebuffer console and then advances to a new line.
Converts a signed integer to decimal characters and prints it.
Fills the complete framebuffer with one RGB colour and resets the text cursor.
Writes one pixel after checking the framebuffer boundaries and active clipping rectangle.
Copies two strings into a rotating runtime buffer and returns the combined text.
Compares ASCII letters without treating uppercase and lowercase as different.
Polls the serial input queue and reports whether a complete newline-terminated command is ready.
Returns the latest completed serial line and marks it as consumed.
Returns the number of files GRUB loaded as Multiboot modules.
Returns the boot-module command-line name for an uploaded file.
Returns an uploaded file size in bytes.
Prints an uploaded file as text. Binary files may contain unreadable bytes or embedded zeroes.
Runs the x86 IN instruction. Reading the wrong port can return meaningless data or interfere with hardware.
Runs the x86 OUT instruction. Incorrect writes can freeze the VM or place devices into an unexpected state.
Adds a C comment for people reading the generated source. It has no runtime effect.
